s: The Vital-Vidhvansak, the first monthly journal to have the untouchable people as its target audience was published by
x: Gopal Baba Walangkar was born in 1840 into a Mahar family near Mahad. An ex-army man, he was deeply influenced by Jyotirao Phule and adopted his ideas on social equality. Walangkar supported Phule's Aryan invasion theory and argued that the untouchables were the indigenous inhabitants of India, while the Brahmins were descendants of Aryans who had invaded the country. In 1886, Walangkar established the anti-caste organisation "Anarya Dosh-Parihar Samaj" to address the Dalit issues. In 1888, Walangkar started a monthly journal, Vital-Vidhvansak, which was the first to target the untouchables. He is credited with pioneering Dalit periodicals. Additional Information: In the 19 TH century, educated Indians started several journals. However, most of these were started by Brahmins and did not discuss the challenges faced by Dalits. This led to the emergence of Dalit periodicals, in which Dalits discussed their issues. Gopal Baba Walangkar, Shivram Janba Kamble, Kisan Fagu Bansode and Dr. Ambedkar played an important role in discussing Dalit issues in journals or periodicals. s: Who among the following was the founder of the 'Self-Respect Movement'?
x: The Self Respect Movement (SRM), founded in 1925 by E. V. Ramasamy (Periyar) in Tamil Nadu, was built on earlier Dravidian reform efforts. It aimed to secularise Tamizh society, promote rationalism, and challenge caste hierarchies, laying the foundation for modern Dravidian politics. The movement, called 'Suyamariyathai' or Self- Respect, symbolises the idea that 'Maanam' or honour is a basic human instinct that distinguishes humans from other animals. Periyar identified the notion of self-respect with three other important concepts: ' Samathuvam' (Equality), 'Suthanthiram' (Freedom) and 'Samadharmam' (Communism).
